hypotheses.label: Retrieval-augmented grounding
hypotheses.description: A language model retrieves external passages and conditions its answer on cited evidence.

hypotheses.label: Prompt injection attack
hypotheses.description: Malicious instructions in user or retrieved content attempt to override an agent's intended policy.

hypotheses.label: Model hallucination
hypotheses.description: A generative model produces fluent claims that are unsupported, inconsistent, or factually incorrect.

hypotheses.label: Concept drift
hypotheses.description: The statistical relationship between inputs and target changes after deployment and degrades predictions.

hypotheses.label: Training-data poisoning
hypotheses.description: An adversary corrupts training examples to alter learned behavior or implant a backdoor.

hypotheses.label: Adversarial examples
hypotheses.description: Small test-time input perturbations intentionally cause a trained model to make an incorrect prediction.

hypotheses.label: Catastrophic forgetting
hypotheses.description: Sequential learning on new tasks damages performance on knowledge learned from earlier tasks.

hypotheses.label: Retrieval reranking
hypotheses.description: A second-stage model reorders initially retrieved candidates using richer query-document interactions.

hypotheses.label: Model quantization
hypotheses.description: Weights or activations use lower numerical precision to reduce memory, latency, and energy.

hypotheses.label: Mixture-of-experts routing
hypotheses.description: A learned router activates a sparse subset of specialized neural experts for each token or example.

hypotheses.label: Reinforcement learning from human feedback
hypotheses.description: Human preference data trains a reward signal used to align a model's responses.

hypotheses.label: Tool-calling AI agent
hypotheses.description: A model selects structured actions and invokes external tools while maintaining an execution loop.

hypotheses.label: Multi-agent coordination
hypotheses.description: Multiple specialized agents exchange messages, delegate work, and resolve dependencies toward a shared goal.

hypotheses.label: Embedding drift
hypotheses.description: Changes in encoder versions or input populations move vector distributions and damage similarity retrieval.

hypotheses.label: Differential privacy
hypotheses.description: Randomized mechanisms bound how much any individual's data can affect a released result or model.

hypotheses.label: Federated learning
hypotheses.description: Clients train locally and aggregate model updates without centralizing their raw data.

hypotheses.label: Knowledge distillation
hypotheses.description: A smaller student model learns from softened predictions or representations produced by a larger teacher.

hypotheses.label: LLM evaluation
hypotheses.description: A measurement protocol assesses model quality, safety, calibration, cost, and robustness on defined tasks.

hypotheses.label: Context-window limitation
hypotheses.description: A model's finite token budget limits how much conversation or retrieved material can be processed at once.

hypotheses.label: Cost-aware LLM routing
hypotheses.description: A policy sends each task to a model tier that balances expected quality, latency, and monetary cost.
